title: Cairo to Luxor Sleeper Train: How to Book (2026)
excerpt: The Cairo to Luxor sleeper train is run by Abela and leaves from Bashtil station: current timetable, cabins, fares from US$110 and how to book.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

The quick answer

The Cairo to Luxor sleeper train is run by Abela Trains, the service many guides still call Watania, and it leaves from Cairo Upper Egypt station at Bashtil (also written Bashteel), not Ramses. Book on abelatrains.com, through the Abela app, at an Abela ticket office or through an agency. Foreigner fares in 2026 start at US$110 per person sharing a standard two-berth cabin, with dinner and breakfast included (Seat 61, checked 8 November 2026). Reserve early: bookings open four to five months ahead and berths sell out in high season.

Check Abela Trains directly for current sleeper services, departure stations, fares and booking availability.

Key facts

Fact Detail
Route Overnight sleeper from Cairo to Luxor; the same trains continue to Aswan

Departs Train 86 daily from Cairo Upper Egypt (Bashtil) at 19:45, calling at Giza at 20:15; train 82 daily at 21:10 and 21:40 (2026 timetable)
Arrives Train 86 reaches Luxor at 06:10 and Aswan at 09:25; train 82 reaches Luxor at 07:50 and Aswan at 11:10
Cabin classes Elite and Standard, each with one-berth and two-berth cabins

Booking abelatrains.com and the Abela app, Abela offices at Ramses, Cairo Upper Egypt, Giza, Luxor and Aswan, or agencies such as Trains Egypt, 12Go and Bookaway
Flight alternative Cairo to Luxor flies in about 1 hour 5 minutes to 1 hour 10 minutes
Join it on Sawa Egypt in Depth: 9-Day Nile Cruise & Cairo, with domestic flights included instead of the train

You want to reach Luxor overnight, but every search result about the Cairo to Luxor sleeper train contradicts the last: Abela or Watania? Ramses or Bashtil? Most pages are out of date. The operator changed in 2023 and the departure station changed after Bashtil station opened in late 2024. This post gives the current picture: who runs the train, where it leaves, what the cabins are like, what it costs and how to book without surprises. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is an Egypt shared-departure marketplace, and its team has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Cairo to Luxor sleeper train: the short answer

Yes, the overnight sleeper still runs and remains the classic way south: dinner on the rails, a cabin bed, and a 06:10 arrival in Luxor on the quickest service. Two things most older articles get wrong: the operator is now Abela Trains, not Watania, and the train leaves from Bashtil, not Ramses. A shared standard cabin with dinner and breakfast costs US$110 per person one way (Seat 61, 2026 fares, page last updated 14 September 2026; check abelatrains.com on the day you book, because fares are set in hard currency and have moved before).

Who runs the sleeper now: Abela or Watania?

Abela Trains runs Egypt's Cairo to Luxor to Aswan sleepers. Abela Egypt won the sleeper-train management contract in October 2022, was granted the rights in January 2023 for 15 years, and took over operation and management from the National Sleeping Trains Company in August 2023, according to Ahram Online (2 August 2023). Before that the same trains ran as the Watania Sleeping Trains, hence the outdated Watania references in guides, forums and ticket pages. Same route, new operator, new booking site: abelatrains.com.

Ignore sources that still send you to Watania for bookings. Book only through abelatrains.com, the Abela app, an Abela ticket office or a reputable agency.

Which station does the sleeper leave from: Bashtil or Ramses?

The sleeper departs from Cairo Upper Egypt station at Bashtil, a terminal in the Bashteel district of Giza governorate, in the west of Greater Cairo. It was inaugurated on 12 October 2024 and opened to passengers on 7 November 2024. Seat 61 says the sleepers no longer leave from Ramses, although Abela still sells tickets there. Bashtil has no direct metro link, so plan a taxi or ride-hail and allow generous time for Cairo traffic.

  • Giza is the other boarding point. The train calls at Giza about 30 minutes after Bashtil, and Giza station can be reached by metro, which suits travellers staying near the pyramids.
  • Northbound arrivals differ. Train 83 arrives at Giza at 05:10 and Cairo Ramses at 05:30, while train 87 arrives at Giza at 06:05 and Cairo Upper Egypt at 06:25. Check which station your return ticket names.
  • Check your platform on the day. The station is new, so confirm your carriage with the attendant before boarding, and bring water and snacks for the wait.

How do I book the Cairo to Luxor sleeper train?

Booking is straightforward if you use the right channel. Seat 61 says booking for the Abela sleepers opens four to five months ahead, although this varies, and berths sell out in peak season.

  1. Choose your train and cabin. Train 86 leaves Bashtil at 19:45 (Giza 20:15) and reaches Luxor at 06:10. Train 82 leaves at 21:10 and reaches Luxor at 07:50. Share a two-berth cabin or pay more for sole occupancy.
  2. Book on abelatrains.com or the Abela app. Seat 61 calls the website slow and quirky and says the app often works better. On the site, choose "Bed Elite class" or "Bed Standard class", and pick "Upper Egypt" or "Giza" as your Cairo station rather than plain "Cairo".
  3. Or use an agency. Trains Egypt, 12Go and Bookaway all sell the sleepers. Seat 61 notes that agencies do not always make clear whether you are getting Elite or Standard, and that Trains Egypt does not book to or from Giza, Kom Ombo or Edfu. Expect an agency margin.
  4. Or book by phone or in person. Abela's reservations line is open 09:00 to 15:00 Egyptian time daily except Fridays, and the offices at Ramses, Cairo Upper Egypt, Giza, Luxor and Aswan take foreign currency and credit cards.
  5. Settle in. Dinner and breakfast are served in the compartment. Carry small notes for tips.

What are the cabins like? Elite vs Standard sleeper

Every cabin is private, with upper and lower berths, clean bedding, a towel, soap and a washbasin. A solo traveller can book a one-berth cabin, or one bed in a two-berth cabin shared with a passenger of the same gender. There is also a club car that sells tea, coffee and soft drinks but no alcohol.

Elite sleeper Standard sleeper
Power A two-pin socket near each berth No sockets confirmed
Fare, sharing (one way, 2026) US$125 per person US$110 per person
Fare, sole occupancy (one way, 2026) US$170 US$150
Best for Travellers who want to charge phones and cameras overnight Budget travellers

The difference is US$15 per person sharing and US$20 sole. If a power socket by your bed matters, pay it; otherwise Standard gives you the same route, the same evening meal and the same breakfast.

How much does the sleeper train cost in 2026?

Foreigner fares are set in US dollars and priced separately from Egyptian fares, a system in place since December 2022. The 2026 one-way fares published by Seat 61 are below. Cairo to Luxor and Cairo to Aswan cost the same, which means Luxor is no cheaper than going on to Aswan. Agencies add their margin.

Fare type, one way (Seat 61, 2026) Price per person
Standard cabin, shared two-berth US$110
Standard cabin, sole occupancy US$150
Elite cabin, shared two-berth US$125
Elite cabin, sole occupancy US$170
Child aged 4 to 9 US$70
Under 4, without a berth Free
Luxor to Aswan on trains 86 and 87, seats only US$10

The fare buys transport, an evening meal, breakfast and a night you do not pay a hotel for. Other websites quote lower figures from earlier years, so treat anything undated with caution and confirm on abelatrains.com when you book.

Sleeper train vs flying to Luxor: which should you choose?

Fly when time matters; take the sleeper when the experience and the hotel saving matter. A domestic flight takes about 1 hour 5 minutes to 1 hour 10 minutes in the air, but it adds airport transfers and a hotel night, and the sleeper replaces a night's accommodation at the cost of morning energy.

Sleeper train Flight
Time Evening to morning, about 10.5 hours on train 86, with a bed included About 1 hour in the air, plus transfers and security
Cost, one way From US$110 with dinner and breakfast (Seat 61, 2026) An aggregator (12Go) listed flights from about US$88 to US$327 on 8 November 2026; airline fares differ
Hotel night in Luxor Not needed on arrival Needed on arrival
Experience Dinner, a bed, sunrise over the Nile Fast, no views of Middle Egypt
Best for Slow itineraries, couples, hotel savers Tight schedules, families with small children

If your Cairo evenings are spoken for, take the sleeper: you trade a wasted travel day for a dinner, a bed and an early arrival. With four days in Egypt in total, fly and start sightseeing by noon.

How to do Cairo and Luxor with Sawa Tours

The sleeper covers the leg; Sawa covers the days. Sawa Tours does not sell train tickets, and it is a marketplace, not a rail agent: you book the train through Abela or an agency. What Sawa runs is a fixed catalogue of shared departures, each operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. The Egypt in Depth: 9-Day Nile Cruise & Cairo package, from €1,403 per person, as listed in November 2026, includes the domestic flights between Cairo and Luxor and between Aswan and Cairo instead of the train, four Cairo nights and four nights on a Nile cruise from Luxor to Aswan, in three comfort tiers, with a guide. It departs on Wednesdays and Fridays; your group of up to 8 sails on a shared five-star ship and does the excursions together with its guide. The Luxor in Depth full-day tour (from €75 per person, as listed in November 2026) includes hotel pickup and starts early, so after an early-morning arrival by sleeper it is better booked for the following day.

Reserving a seat on any departure is free, with no card, and nothing is charged before the GoAhead, the moment four travellers (people, not bookings) have reserved the date. Groups never exceed eight; when a date fills, a new independent departure opens. Payment is by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros.

  • Day tours: a 10% deposit at the GoAhead, the balance two days (48 hours) before departure. A forming date has until seven days before to reach four. Cancel at least 48 hours before for a full refund; under 48 hours you lose the 10% deposit.
  • Packages and cruises: a 25% deposit at the GoAhead, the balance 14 days before departure, and the date must reach four by 30 days before. Cancelling 30 or more days before costs nothing; 29 to 15 days before costs half the deposit (12.5%); 14 days or fewer, or a no-show, and the deposit (25%) is retained. Some components, such as flights and cabins, may become non-refundable earlier, and this is disclosed before you pay.

See how the GoAhead works, the GoAhead promise and the terms, and browse forming departures.

The takeaway

The sleeper remains a smart Cairo to Luxor move, but book it in the present tense: Abela Trains runs it, Bashtil station hosts it, and a cabin costs from US$110 with dinner and breakfast included (Seat 61, 2026 fares). Reserve early, reach Bashtil with time to spare, and browse forming Sawa departures for guided days in Luxor.

faq.q: Is the overnight train to Luxor safe for solo travellers?
faq.a: Cabins are private compartments, and a solo traveller can book a one-berth cabin or one bed in a two-berth cabin shared with a passenger of the same gender. Keep valuables with you and confirm your platform at Bashtil. As with any rail travel in Egypt, the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) notes that fatal train collisions and derailments have occurred, so this is a normal-risk journey, not a risk-free one.

faq.q: Are meals included on the Cairo to Luxor night train?
faq.a: Yes. The fare includes an evening meal tray and a breakfast with an omelette and tea or coffee, served in the compartment. The club car sells tea, coffee and soft drinks but no alcohol. Options are simple, so bring snacks if you have dietary restrictions.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book sleeper train tickets?
faq.a: As early as the booking window allows: Seat 61 says it opens four to five months ahead, although this varies. Cabins go first in the October to April high season and over Christmas and Easter. Agency bookings need at least two days' notice.

faq.q: What if the sleeper train is sold out on my date?
faq.a: Switch transport, not the day. Domestic flights from Cairo to Luxor take about an hour, and daytime trains also run the route, taking about 10 to 11 hours. Check abelatrains.com, the app and one agency before concluding a date is full, because inventories differ.

faq.q: Can Sawa book my Cairo to Luxor sleeper train ticket?
faq.a: No. Sawa Tours is a shared-departure platform for guided tours and packages, not a rail agent. Where Sawa helps: the Egypt in Depth package includes domestic flights instead of the train, and shared Luxor day tours can be booked for the day after you arrive. If you combine separate departures, book flights and trains only after each date confirms.

faq.q: What happens if the Sawa departure I join doesn't fill?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. A date confirms when four travellers have reserved it, and the deposit (10% on a day tour, 25% on a package) is taken only then. A day tour has until seven days before departure to reach four, and a package until 30 days before; if a date misses, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and Sawa suggests another date. Once confirmed, a departure is not cancelled for low numbers, and a traveller who does not pay the balance is excluded while the tour still runs. More in the FAQ .

faq.q: Do children pay full fare on the sleeper train?
faq.a: Children aged 4 to 9 pay a reduced fare of US$70 one way (Seat 61, 2026), and children under 4 travel free but without a berth. If a young child needs a bed, they pay the child rate. Cabins are one or two berths, so a family of four books two cabins; ask for adjoining cabins when booking.
